author: Jeff Graham
title: Olympic College adding building in Bremerton as innovation, tech hub - NewsBreak
text:
By Jeff Graham ,
1 days ago BREMERTON — Olympic College will begin transforming a fairly ordinary piece of property on the west side of campus, mainly grass and an asphalt parking lot, into its new hub for computer science-related programming later this year.
Plans for OC's 31,864-square foot Innovation & Technology Center are underway with the two-story building destined to be built on a portion of Lot 12, located between 14th and 15th Streets along Ohio Avenue. The area is previously where the college's theater stood before construction moved arts and health sciences to the northeast portion of campus in 2018.
OC is working with the city of Bremerton on obtaining all the necessary permitting prior to putting the project out to bid.
"We're funded and we'll be breaking ground this coming fall," said Shawn Devine, OC's chief communications officer during a brief campus tour Monday, April 6.
The target completion date is April 2028 and the building is scheduled to open June 2028. The new venue will accommodate up to 23 faculty/staff and 258 students at peak occupancy. Programming will include computer information systems, computer science, cybersecurity, digital media arts and makerspaces.
"It's really going to be an IT hub," said Devine, who noted that Port Orchard artist Matthew Olds will contribute to the finished product by adding a yet-to-be-determined aesthetic element, such as a mural or sculpture.
The total cost of the project is $34,584,028 and covers furniture and architecture fees. Olympic College secured funding as part of the Washington State Board for Community & Technical College's 2025-27 biennium capital funding budget.
Olympic College initially identified plans for a centralized innovation and technology building in 2013 while updating its Bremerton campus master plan. Currently, most computer science classes are taught in Building 12, which houses the college's business and information technology divisions.
This article originally appeared on Kitsap Sun: Olympic College adding building in Bremerton as innovation, tech hub
